intent.raw: Implement the correction that the ontology product is Ontology-as-a-Product and show the final result.
intent.objective: Author and validate a successor migration architecture that separates Product, Product Ontology, ontology-package output, contexts, Craft, capabilities, and runtimes.

subagent_strategy.explanation: One bounded successor package and deterministic validation do not require delegated agents.

steps.name: Resolve Product and Ontology definition authority
stop_conditions: stop if Product or Ontology meaning cannot be resolved

steps.name: Distill Product, Product Ontology, and output identities
convergence_criteria: smallest unit recomposes into the migration
stop_conditions: stop if a generated label is required as a new canonical axis

steps.name: Author successor migration plan
stop_conditions: stop if the plan mutates predecessor evidence or requests an intermediate approval

steps.name: Validate semantic model, plan, dispatch, and projections
stop_conditions: stop on source, identity, non-collapse, projection, approval-boundary, or dispatch failure

gates.condition: Product and Ontology bind canonical meanings while dependent labels remain generated projections.
Product, Product Ontology, ontology-package output, Craft, contexts, capabilities, and runtimes remain distinct.
Only the immutable L4 end-to-end candidate may request Product approval; all authority effects remain later and separate.

boundaries.contract: Reference canonical definitions and express dependent labels through relations; planning prose cannot create normative meaning.
Bind exact predecessor plan, dispatch, and receipt digests without rewriting them.

authority.lifecycle: respective Definition, Product, Context, Context Map, artifact-type, and runtime owners
authority.promotion: human Product decision owner after L4 only

promotion_guardrails: Generated labels cannot create canonical axes.
A Product Ontology cannot become the Product or its delivered output by placement or naming.
Plan PASS cannot clear source drift, admit artifacts, approve the Product, or authorize operational effects.
